espn-604593.headline: Jake White starts where Fiji's title slipped away
beats: Five weeks ago on this ground Japan beat Fiji 20–15 in the Pacific Nations Cup final. Fiji have since hired Jake White, South Africa's 2007 World Cup-winning coach. His first game is the same opponent in the same place.
The rankings make it sharper. A Fiji win lifts them to ninth, above Japan. Whoever loses falls below Wales and Italy, twelfth at best.

Form says Japan: three straight wins, including 63–14 against the USA and 57–12 against Canada. Fiji have won once in five tests this year. A year earlier they beat Japan 33–27 in the final in Salt Lake City.
White, 62, was picked from 31 applicants. His former Bulls backline coach, Chris Rossouw, offers the forecast: “I wouldn’t be surprised if they’re going to surprise people.”
A fortnight later both are in Europe, Japan away to Wales and Fiji away to France.

sources.title: World Cup-winning coach White takes reins at Fiji
